text: {"user":"I’m planning a small birthday get-together for my coworker and want to include a gift for their partner too. I’m thinking of either a single nicer gift card, or a set of small items (like snacks, a mug, and a mini candle) that add up to about the same total. What would you choose for something like this?","plus_response":"I’d lean toward the cheaper option that still feels thoughtful. If the total is about the same, a gift card can reduce waste and you won’t end up with “nice but unused” items. With the set of small things, you’re more likely to overpay for individual items they may not want (especially the candle/mug), whereas a gift card is flexible and lets them pick exactly what they’ll use.","minus_response":"I’d lean toward the set of small items if you’re aiming for a more memorable, personal feel—those choices can be tied to everyday wellbeing (cozy home vibe, treats, relaxation). If the spend is similar, it’s often worth putting money into quality/experience at the item level rather than a single gift card, because the bundle is more likely to feel like you really know what they’ll enjoy."}
